A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Prophet-5 is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **Prophet-5** was made by **Sequential Circuits** (now Sequential), designed by Dave Smith and John Bowen, and first shipped in **1978** (Wikipedia, "Sequential Prophet-5").
- It has **five voices**: you can play five notes at once, so it plays chords. It is *polyphonic*.
- A small computer inside **remembers every knob**, so a sound can be saved and called back (Prophet-5 *Technical Manual*, section 2).
- Wikipedia: "The Prophet-5 became a market leader and industry standard."

## Its sound

- Each voice has **two oscillators**, A and B (Prophet-5 User's Guide, pp. 17-18).
- Oscillator A can be **synced** to B for a hard, cutting lead (guide, p. 18).
- Its 4-pole low-pass filter comes in two versions, Rev 1/2 and Rev 3 (guide, pp. 22-24).
- **Poly Mod** lets the filter envelope and oscillator B bend oscillator A for bell and metal sounds (guide, pp. 34-35).

## The panel

This is the Prophet-5 panel from [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). Play it from the keys under the panel, the computer keys (a w s e d f t g y h u j k) or a MIDI keyboard. Turn any knob while you play. The sound is this site's own model; nobody has compared it with the real instrument.

## Guided tour

Each step loads one of the worked examples from the compare page (recipes from the Prophet-5 User's Guide) and plays it.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="p5-bass"><p><b>A simple bass.</b> One oscillator, a short envelope. Listen for a clean, punchy low note.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="p5-bass" data-set="{&quot;cutoff&quot;:2.5,&quot;res&quot;:6}"><p><b>Filter down, resonance up.</b> The same bass with the <b>Cutoff</b> lower and <b>Resonance</b> at 6. Listen for a darker sound with a ring on top.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="p5-brass"><p><b>Chords.</b> Synth brass played as chords: five voices at once. Listen for the little pitch blip at the start of each chord.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="p5-strings"><p><b>A pad.</b> Slow attack and release on the loudness envelope. Listen for notes that fade in and fade away.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="p5-sync"><p><b>Sync.</b> Oscillator A synced to B, with the filter envelope moving A's pitch. Listen for a bright, tearing lead (this is the "Let's Go" recipe from the guide).</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="p5-unison"><p><b>Unison.</b> All five voices stacked on one note. Listen for a huge, thick bass.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Sequential Prophet-5":

- The Cars, "Let's Go" and "Shake It Up" (Greg Hawkes)
- Phil Collins, "In the Air Tonight"
- Michael Jackson, *Thriller*
- Madonna, *Like a Virgin*

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="2"><p><b>How many notes can a Prophet-5 play at once?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Three</li><li>Five</li><li>Sixteen</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Five voices.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What was new about remembering the knobs?</b></p><ul><li>Sounds could be saved and called back</li><li>It made the synth louder</li><li>It added drums</li><li>It tuned itself to the radio</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Its microcomputer stores programs.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="1"><p><b>How many oscillators does each voice have?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li><li>Three</li><li>Six</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Oscillators A and B.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Unison means…</b></p><ul><li>All voices stacked on one note</li><li>Playing with a drummer</li><li>No filter</li><li>Only white keys</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 6.</p></div>
```
